title: Generic flatness for a finite type morphism to an integral scheme
statement: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes, with $S$ integral (nonempty, reduced and irreducible), and $f$ locally of finite type and quasi-compact. There is a nonempty open subset $U \subseteq S$ such that the induced morphism $f^{-1}(U) \to U$ is flat.

source.place: Tag 052A, Proposition generic flatness, applied to the structure sheaf; Tag 051T, finite type algebra generic freeness

proof.text: Choose a point of the nonempty integral base and an affine-cover open V containing it. The open subscheme V is affine and integral. Restrict f to V; local finite type and quasi-compactness are preserved. The inverse image of V is quasi-compact because V is affine, so its affine cover has a finite subcover.

Apply the affine-chart lemma to each component of the finite affine source cover, obtaining nonzero sections a_i of the affine base and flatness over D(a_i). Each D(a_i) is nonempty because the integral base is reduced and a_i is nonzero; hence each contains its generic point. The finite intersection U of these basic opens is open and contains that generic point, including when the index set is empty.

Restrict each flat chart further from D(a_i) to U, using the canonical isomorphism for nested restrictions. Pull back the finite source cover along the inclusion of f^{-1}(U). The pullback-symmetry and restriction isomorphisms identify its component maps with the restricted flat chart maps. Flatness is local at the source, so f restricted to U is flat. Finally push U into S along V.ι; its image is nonempty, and morphismRestrictRestrict transports flatness to the restriction of the original f to that image.

proof_origin.place: Tag 052A, affine finite-cover argument; Tag 051T through lem-sbc-finite-type-algebra-generic-flatness
proof_origin.note: The Lean proof uses a finite intersection of basic opens instead of their product and proves all geometric reduction and gluing steps. Only the coordinate-algebra generic-flatness step remains as a named theorem.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_nonempty_open_flat_restrict {X S : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral S]
    (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] :
    ∃ U : S.Opens, (U : Set S).Nonempty ∧ Flat (f ∣_ U)
